provenance.rule: dominant cell = max memberCount; elite = cell.eliteWalker
provenance.dominantCellDescriptor: cardinality=5-6 | primary-layout-carrier=family (role/tier directory) | depth=3 | generated-in-vcs=yes (mostly; a few partial/dual-track) | unit-kind=package | repo-count=1
provenance.contents: eliteSummary + designQuestions + classifications + layoutSketch + probeClassifications, verbatim from walker 35; trajectory and selfScores deliberately excluded (1a instrument artefacts, not the design)

draw.constraint: optimise exclusively for AI-agent token economics (cost to find, read, and safely edit)

eliteSummary: The dominant convergence shape across personas: 5-6 near-orthogonal classifications (license/edit-domain/import-boundary/quality-gate/consumption/domain or close variants), carried by a tiered directory family (core→infrastructure→products, license root-split), generated bytes committed under a /data or /generated subtree. Elite (walker 35) pairs this with explicit license+edit-domain root partition and .generation.yaml regeneration manifests, zero forced fits.

classifications.name: Generation Origin
classifications.question: Where does the source code come from?
classifications.carrier: Inferred from source; declared in package.json via regenerationTrigger field

classifications.name: Consumer Class
classifications.question: Who consumes this unit and under what contract?
classifications.values: Published (npm) | Internal (workspace) | Demo (published but non-product) | Research (isolated) | Operational (tooling)
classifications.carrier: package.json privateFlag and publishConfig; ESLint boundary rules

classifications.name: Change Rhythm
classifications.question: How often and by what trigger does this unit change?
classifications.carrier: package.json regenerationTrigger field; CI hook naming convention

classifications.name: Edit Boundary
classifications.question: Which bytes may humans edit, and which are machine-only?
classifications.carrier: .gitignore patterns; package.json editBoundary field; ESLint orphan exceptions

classifications.name: Licensing
classifications.question: Under what terms may this unit be reused externally?
classifications.carrier: package.json license field; exports map declares per-path license; LICENCE file for edge cases

classifications.name: Stability/Publication Stage
classifications.question: Is this unit mature/stable, or experimental/temporary?
classifications.values: Stable (SemVer, back-compat) | Experimental (rapid iteration) | Demonstration (non-product) | Infrastructure (version drift ok) | Research (temporary)
classifications.carrier: package.json version field (0.x vs 1.x); README classification; ESLint import rules

"
designQuestions: What makes two things SEPARATE units? (differentiation by generation origin, consumer class, edit permission, change coordination)
WHERE does a unit live and how does a newcomer find it? (hierarchical path: layer/audience/concern/name; discovery via package.json, README, dependency graph)
Who may IMPORT whom? (unidirectional flow: core ← libs ← sdks/apps ← demos; research/ops/plugins isolated)
Who may EDIT which bytes, and what regenerates? (EditBoundary field in package.json; regenerationTrigger declares automated refresh points)
Under what LICENSE each unit may travel or be reused? (MIT for code; OGL-v3.0 for content; Brand-reserved for assets; mixed via exports map)
What does CHANGING the organization cost? (path changes O(n) rewrites; layer changes very expensive; license elevation requires audit; regeneration changes are contained)
